FOOTNOTES

1/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$531,900 and 5 FTE Positions from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Adult Workforce Diploma Program Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding from the General Fund in FY 2027 for an Adult Workforce Diploma Program Fund Deposit. Adjustments are as follows:
section_path: Adult Workforce Diploma Program Fund Deposit

text:
Remove One-Time Deposit

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(2,000,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove a one-time deposit into the Adult Workforce Diploma Program Fund.

The Adult Workforce Diploma Program and monies in the Adult Workforce Diploma Program Fund are for making payments to approved providers in the Adult Workforce Diploma Program of \$1,000 per recipient that earns a high school diploma and lower awards for other specified program milestones. Program providers may offer services online, a campus-based program, or a blended format. OEO may retain up to 5% of the monies in the fund to administer the Adult Workforce Diploma Program.

The Adult Workforce Diploma Program and Adult Workforce Diploma Program Fund were established by Laws 2022, Chapter 317 and originally administered by the Department of Education (ADE). The FY 2026 K-12 Education Budget Reconciliation Bill (BRB) transferred the program to OEO and created a new fund. A General Appropriations Act footnote required all monies remaining in the original fund to be transferred to the new Adult Workforce Diploma Program Fund at the end of FY 2025.

Other adult education programs are administered by ADE, including the Continuing High School and Workforce Training Program and the Community College Adult Education Workforce Development Program. (Please see the ADE section for more details.)

Dual Enrollment Student Development Program

The Baseline includes no funding from the General Fund in FY 2027 for the Dual Enrollment Student Development Program. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Funding

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,500,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 to remove one-time funding for the Dual Enrollment Student Development Program.

An FY 2026 General Appropriations Act footnote requires the one-time funding to be distributed by the Office of Economic Opportunity to community college dual enrollment programs, with a priority to serve students who qualify for free and reduced-price lunch. The Office of Economic Opportunity may retain up to 3% of the appropriated amount for administration. The Dual Enrollment Student Development program was originally established in ADE and received one-time funding in the FY 2024 budget.

Agency Structure and Funding

Laws 2016, Chapter 372 created 3 new governmental entities: The Office of Economic Opportunity (OEO), the Arizona Finance Authority (AFA), and the Arizona Industrial Development Authority (AIDA). AFA is established in OEO and the AFA board serves as the board of AIDA, thus OEO has statutory supervision over all 3 entities. (Please see the FY 2020 Appropriations Report for more details.)

OEO

OEO is the central state agency for economic, population, and unemployment statistical analysis, serves as the administering agency for the Workforce Arizona Council, and oversees the Workforce Data Task Force.

AFA

AFA houses the functions of the Greater Arizona Development Authority (GADA) and administers the state’s Private Activity Bond (PAB) authorization.

AIDA

AFA also governs AIDA, which has responsibility for the former activities for the Arizona Housing Finance Authority, Arizona Health Facilities Authority, and the Arizona International Development Authority. In addition, AIDA is authorized to issue PABs for allowable projects not otherwise covered by the other state IDAs.

Purpose of Fund: To fund the operations of AFA. Oversees the state’s private activity bond authorization and the operations of WIFA and GADA.

Greater Arizona Development Authority Revolving Fund (FAA2311/A.R.S. § 41-2254) Non-Appropriated

Source of Revenue: Legislative appropriations, federal monies, gifts, grants, donations, loan repayments, administrative fees and penalties, and interest.

Purpose of Fund: To help rural communities meet their infrastructure needs. GADA may issue bonds, guarantee debt obligations, and provide technical and financial assistance to political subdivisions, special districts, and Indian tribes. Legislative appropriations to the GADA Revolving Fund may only be used to secure bonds. The state funding only serves as collateral for the loans and is not directly loaned out. The fund was capitalized with \$20,000,000 from the General Fund between FY 1998 and FY 2000. Other revenue to the fund may be used for GADA's operating costs, as well as technical and financial assistance to communities. The expenditures displayed below represent administrative costs.
